passage:
Ella's ruler broke during a math test. She raised her hand, but the teacher had no extra ruler.
A student behind her, Paul, quietly passed his ruler forward. Ella used it and returned it after the test.
Later, Paul found that he had not finished one question because he waited for the ruler to come back. Ella felt terrible when she heard this.
Paul said, "It's fine. I chose to help."
The next day, Ella brought two rulers to school. She gave one to Paul and kept one in her pencil box.
She learned that help can cost something, even when the helper does not complain. Saying thank you is good, but remembering the cost of kindness is better.
